newsitem.title: GERMANY: Telekom to quit MMBG television joint venture - paper.
newsitem.headline: Telekom to quit MMBG television joint venture - paper.

text.p: German state-owned telephone company Deutsche Telekom AG plans to quit the MMBG digital television venture it formed with public and private sector broadcasters, Sueddeutsche Zeitung reported on Monday.
Telekom planned to market television programmes independently in future, the report said.
Telekom is the largest shareholder in MMBG, or Multimedia Betriebs GmbH, with a 27 percent stake.

MMBG shareholders include Deutsche Telekom with 27 percent, German publishing giant Bertelsmann AG, French pay TV group Canal Plus, German commercial TV broadcaster RTL and public broadcasters ARD and ZDF.

The spokesman was commenting on a report in the Sueddeutsche Zeitung newspaper which said Telekom wanted to try and make its cable television operation profitable by offering digital pay TV to its 5.5 million subscribers.
The move is a further blow to Bertelsmann's plans to play a dominant role in the German pay TV market, after it has been outpaced by Bavarian media mogul Leo Kirch.
Canal Plus, Bertelsmann's partner so far in pay TV company Premiere, also recently took over Dutch pay TV group Nethold to become one of the world's largest operators in the sector.
Bertelsmann has yet to launch digital TV programming, but remains through its TV merger with Compagnie Luxembourgeoise de Telediffusion CLT, Europe's largest free TV broadcasting group.
